description: Goodyear, AZ homes with Teigh Wade, REALTOR®: Estrella, PebbleCreek (55+), Palm Valley, I-10 and Loop 303 access, water providers by area and HOA checks.
summary: Goodyear is an incorporated city in Maricopa County's southwest Valley, split by I-10 and anchored by Loop 303. Most homes are in master-planned communities such as Estrella south of the freeway and Palm Valley and PebbleCreek, which is 55+, to the north. HOAs are standard. Teigh Wade, REALTOR®, helps clients buy and sell in Goodyear.

sections.h2: From cotton fields to master plans
sections.html:
Goodyear takes its name from the Goodyear Tire and Rubber Company, which bought 16,000 acres here in 1917 to grow cotton for tire cords. The settlement became a town in 1946 and a city in 1985. During World War II, a Luke Field auxiliary airfield operated here as well. Phoenix Goodyear Airport, which took its current name in 1986, handles aircraft maintenance and storage rather than passenger flights.

Modern Goodyear is defined by master-planned communities. More than twenty have been completed or are under way, with more planned, which means much of the city's housing is relatively new and organized around community associations, parks, trails and amenity centers.

sections.h2: North of I-10 versus south of I-10
sections.html:
Interstate 10 divides Goodyear into two distinct halves, and the split affects more than the commute.

North of the freeway

The northern half includes Palm Valley, a roughly 9,000-acre master plan with a range of home sizes, and PebbleCreek. PebbleCreek, near I-10 and the Loop 303 corridor, is on this side as well. Water here comes from EPCOR or Liberty Utilities, depending on the location.

South of the freeway

The southern half stretches toward the Estrella Mountains and holds Estrella, the city's largest master plan, along with Estrella Mountain Regional Park. Water south of I-10 comes from the City of Goodyear. Maricopa County Highway 85 runs through the southern sections.

Estrella

Estrella covers about 20,000 acres in the foothills of the Sierra Estrella. It has 72 acres of lakes and parks, the Yacht Club of Estrella, the Estrella Lakeside Amphitheater, the Golf Club of Estrella and dozens of miles of trails. Neighborhoods within it include Estrella Mountain Ranch, Montecito and CantaMia, which offers 55+ homes. Development began in the late 1980s and continues today, so build years range widely.

PebbleCreek

PebbleCreek is a gated 55+ active adult community by Robson, with homes built from 1994 to the present. It has two championship golf courses, Eagle's Nest and Tuscany Falls, plus clubhouses, a performing arts center, indoor and outdoor pools, an arts center and courts for tennis, pickleball and bocce. Both detached homes and attached villa homes are available.

Palm Valley

Palm Valley is a master plan of roughly 9,000 acres north of I-10, with many separate neighborhoods and a range of home sizes. Because it was built in phases, build years and HOA structures differ from one section to the next.

• Goodyear Ballpark opened in 2009 as the spring training home of the Cleveland Guardians and Cincinnati Reds.
  • Estrella Mountain Regional Park covers nearly 20,000 acres, mostly desert, with more than 30 miles of trails.
  • Phoenix Goodyear Airport has an 8,500-foot runway used for maintenance and storage of large jets.
  • The lakes and amphitheater in Estrella host community events.

• Water provider. Know which side of I-10 the home is on, and confirm whether it is served by the City of Goodyear, EPCOR or Liberty Utilities. Rates and conservation rules can differ.
  • HOA layers. Master plans often have a master HOA plus a village or neighborhood association, and gated or golf communities may add fees. Ask for every set of documents and any fees at closing.
  • Age rules. PebbleCreek and CantaMia are 55+. Confirm eligibility before you write an offer.
  • Solar. Owned systems transfer with the home; leased or financed systems need the solar company's approval.
  • Pools. Order a separate pool inspection.
  • New construction. When comparing a resale home with a new build, look at lot premiums, upgrade costs, landscaping and window coverings that may not be included.

Electricity in Goodyear comes from APS and natural gas from Southwest Gas. Learn how Teigh handles each step on her buying with Teigh page.

I-10 runs east-west through Goodyear toward downtown Phoenix and west toward Buckeye and California. Loop 303 begins at I-10 in Goodyear and runs north toward Surprise and I-17. Estrella Parkway, Litchfield Road and Bullard Avenue are main north-south roads, and MC-85 serves the south. State Route 30 is a proposed future highway south of I-10.

Goodyear is served by several elementary districts, including Avondale, Liberty, Litchfield and Mobile elementary districts, and by Agua Fria Union and Buckeye Union high school districts. High schools in the city include Desert Edge, Millennium and Estrella Foothills, and Goodyear High School was built to serve students starting with the 2025 to 2026 school year. Confirm the assigned schools for any address with the district.

Goodyear resale homes often compete with brand-new builder inventory, so condition and presentation matter. Buyers usually ask about HOA dues, water provider, solar ownership, pool equipment, and the age of the roof and AC. In the 55+ communities they also ask about amenity fees and golf memberships.

faqs.a: It depends on which side of I-10 the home is on. South of I-10, the City of Goodyear provides water. North of I-10, EPCOR and Liberty Utilities serve different areas. Confirm the provider for any address, since rates and conservation programs differ. Electricity in Goodyear comes from APS.

Yes. PebbleCreek is a gated 55+ active adult community built by Robson, with homes from 1994 to the present. It has the Eagle's Nest and Tuscany Falls golf courses, clubhouses, a performing arts center, pools and courts. Review the HOA documents and age requirements before you make an offer.

Estrella is Goodyear's largest master-planned community, covering about 20,000 acres south of I-10 in the foothills of the Sierra Estrella. It has lakes, the Yacht Club of Estrella, a lakeside amphitheater, a golf club and miles of trails. Neighborhoods include Estrella Mountain Ranch, Montecito and the 55+ CantaMia.

faqs.q: Who plays spring training at Goodyear Ballpark?
faqs.a: The Cleveland Guardians and Cincinnati Reds hold spring training at Goodyear Ballpark, which opened in 2009 and seats about 10,000. The Arizona Complex League teams for both organizations also play there. The Goodyear Centennials of the Freedom Pro Baseball League have also played there.

Interstate 10 runs east-west through the city, and Loop 303 begins at I-10 in Goodyear and heads north toward Surprise and I-17. Maricopa County Highway 85 serves the southern sections. Estrella Parkway and Litchfield Road are major north-south routes, and State Route 30 is a proposed highway south of I-10.

Goodyear is served by the Avondale, Liberty, Litchfield and Mobile elementary districts, and by the Agua Fria Union and Buckeye Union high school districts. The district depends on the address, so confirm the assigned schools with the district for any home you are considering.

Most do. The city is built largely around master-planned communities, and many have both a master association and a neighborhood association. Gated, golf and 55+ communities can carry extra fees. Teigh requests all HOA documents early so you can review dues, rules and closing fees during your inspection period.

faqs.q: How do I price my Goodyear home?
faqs.a: Start with a comparative market analysis. Goodyear values vary by community, side of I-10, lot, age, condition and upgrades, and resale homes often compete with new construction. Teigh compares your home with recent sales and current listings nearby, then recommends a pricing strategy without guaranteeing a result.
